items.title: Live: Spain and Argentina deadlocked in feisty World Cup final
items.description: Spain is looking to win its second World Cup, taking on four-time and defending champions Argentina at New York/New Jersey Stadium. Follow live.

items.title: One telehealth consult and a doctor prescribed unapproved peptides
items.description: The booming industry selling Australians on treatments to live longer is exploiting significant gaps in health regulation, exposing consumers to risk.

items.title: Australia is making humanoid robots in the midst of its AI reckoning
items.description: Australia this week made an important step forward in grappling with the AI revolution. Meanwhile, in Melbourne a company is making humanoid robots.

items.title: Abbott amplifies Hanson problem for Liberals
items.description: Pauline Hanson's grievance politics is a challenge for Labor, but a splitting headache for the Liberals — compounded by former prime minister Tony Abbott.

items.title: Pauline Hanson 'not backing away' from controversial far-right interview
items.description: The One Nation leader was a guest on the podcast of controversial far-right UK figure Tommy Robinson, where she lamented the end of the White Australia policy.

items.title: For some in Australia, hope is fading and anger is rising
items.description: Sulaiman Zandinan says Australia is amazing. Wendy Newman says people in the bush are "not country bumpkins". The ABC is inviting you to have Your Say about the issues, challenges and opportunities that shape your life in 2026.

items.title: US ally Jordan summons Iranian ambassador after missile strikes
items.description: The US warns its citizens to stay away from air and sea ports at Aqaba in southern Jordan, hours before Israeli authorities announced that Iranian missiles had been launched towards the city.

items.title: Museum wants Holocaust education to create 'a safe Australia for everybody'
items.description: Melbourne Holocaust Museum has had to step up security since 2020 following a rise in incidents that have seen threatening voice messages and hateful comments left online.

items.title: Asylum seekers sent to Nauru by Australia say they are going hungry
items.description: According to a survey of 78 asylum seekers on Nauru, 99 per cent said they were regularly skipping meals because they could not afford to buy enough food, while more than three quarters said they rarely had access to free, clean drinking water.

items.title: Rules to tighten on AI use in decision-making by government departments
items.description: Agencies like Centrelink and Services Australia will have to follow a framework to ensure decision-making is "fair and accurate" if they use AI.

items.title: 'Open door to fraud': European body slams FIFA's World Cup integrity
items.description: Europe's top human rights body hits out at FIFA over the integrity of the World Cup and calls for change before the 2030 tournament.

items.title: Australian baseball's 37yo 'rookie' making national debut at World Cup
items.description: Jess Johnson is one of the feel-good stories of the Australian Women's national baseball team.

items.title: Russia pounds Kyiv in major ballistic missile attack
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia battered Ukraine's capital Kyiv overnight into Sunday local time, with one of its biggest ballistic missile barrages of the war.

items.title: Paramedics told not to take complex cardiac patients to Mersey hospital
items.description: Paramedics have been told to transport complex cardiac patients in Tasmania's north-west to the Launceston General Hospital rather than the local Mersey Community Hospital.

items.title: How can you get the balance right when being online is your job?
items.description: When being across trends in your industry feels like part of your job, it can feel like work never ends. Here's how to protect your free time.

items.title: Try this week's history quiz (we made it an easy one)
items.description: Consider yourself a history buff? Test your smarts on the first Moon landing, John Howard and the Riot Act.

items.title: Race Around the World recap: Catch this week's films
items.description: From Mexican wrestling to Indian slums, catch up on every week seven film from Race Around the World.

items.title: Actor Terence Donovan remembered by son Jason as 'larger than life'
items.description: Jason Donovan has paid tribute to his father who has died at the age of 90 after decades on Australian screens.

items.title: The 'terrifying' lab test results from store-bought bottle of vodka
items.description: Australia's bootleg booze market is booming and an alarming new discovery from a bottle of vodka sold in Melbourne reveals it is turning into a major health problem.

items.title: Concerns for lost health services under sale to Calvary
items.description: Doctors are concerned Tasmanians will be forced to travel interstate for certain procedures if the Hobart Private Hospital is sold to Catholic provider Calvary, but the health minister insists there will be no service gap.

items.title: Special guest dazzles aspiring astronauts at Space Day Out
items.description: Young Australians got one step closer to achieving their space exploration dreams on Sunday when they met a "real-life" astronaut.

items.title: Antonelli extends F1 championship lead, heartbroken Russell crashes out in Belgium
items.description: Kimi Antonelli has extended his lead at the top of the F1 championship standings with victory in the Belgian Grand Prix, with Oscar Piastri overcoming an early knock and George Russell's race ending in heartbreak.

items.title: Bek never thought she would grow old until she left her church behind
items.description: Author Bek Condello says she has not spoken to her friends or family inside the church since she decided to leave.

items.title: Andrew and Tristan Tate arrested on sex trafficking offences
items.description: British prosecutors say they are seeking the extradition of the Tate brothers from the US on rape and sex trafficking charges.

items.title: Expert says new cyber law shows Vic government is out of touch with reality
items.description: Jacinta Allan is pledging nation-leading laws forcing tech giants to reveal the identity of trolls, and make it easier for parents to sue tech giants that cause psychiatric harm to their children.
